newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ackermans to book 1.1 bln Bfr gain in '96.
newsitem.headline: Ackermans to book 1.1 bln Bfr gain in '96.

text.p: Belgian holding company Ackermans & Van Haaren NV said on Wednesday it will book a consolidated capital gain of 1.09 billion Belgian francs in its 1996 accounts resulting from the merger of offshore oil services groups Forasol-Foramer NV and Pride Petroleum Services Inc.
Ackermans said in a statement published in Belgian newspapers it would also acquire an indirect interest of around seven percent in the merged entity Pride/Forasol-Foramer.
Ackerman's final 1996 results would be released on March 25, it added.

Ackermans said Forasol-Foramer NV shareholders, including itself, approved the transfer of its operational units to Pride at an extraordinary general shareholders meeting in Rotterdam on Tuesday. Pride shareholders had approved the deal on March 5.
Pride paid for the units through the issue of 11.1 million Pride shares to Forasol-Foramer and through $132.2 million in cash.
Forasol-Foramer shareholders also approved the company's liquidation, with each shareholder receiving 0.66 of a Pride share and $6.80 in cash.
AvH subsidiary Sertofin BV held 5,005,000 Forasol Foramer shares, giving it the right to 3,303,300 Pride shares and $34,034,000 in cash, Ackermans said.
"The new Pride/Forasol-Foramer group with sales in excess of $470 million canbe considered one of the most important petroleum industry service companies in the world," Ackermans said.
Nasdaq-listed Pride has 237 drilling units, of which 23 are in the Gulf of Mexico, and 204 spread through Argentina, Colombia, Venezuela and Russia.
Forasol-Foramer operated in 20 countries, with various offshort and terrestrial drilling units.
